screening.reason: Analyses resting-state fMRI from the KKI site of ABIDE II for an ASD-vs-control effective connectivity (group-difference) analysis; meets inclusion 2-3.

evidence_spans.text: The subjects were 42 autistic children and 127 age-matched normal children from the ABIDE II dataset.
evidence_spans.claim: Final analysed cohort was 42 ASD and 127 TC children from ABIDE II.

evidence_spans.text: We used the KKI dataset in this study. The KKI dataset collected from 211 children aged 8 to 13 years, including 56 children with ASD and 155 children in the typical controls (TC) group.
evidence_spans.claim: Source was the KKI site of ABIDE II, originally 211 children (56 ASD/155 TC) before exclusions.

evidence_spans.text: a total of 14 children with ASD and 28 TC children were excluded, and the final sample included 42 children with ASD and 127 TC children.
evidence_spans.claim: 14 ASD and 28 TC children were excluded (poor normalization, excessive motion, non-convergence of spDCM), leaving 42 ASD/127 TC.

evidence_spans.text: Then 24 ROIs corresponding to 7 brain networks were selected using the AAL standard brain template provided by the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI).
evidence_spans.claim: 24 spherical ROIs across 7 networks were defined using the AAL atlas.

evidence_spans.text: Data processing was performed with the GRETNA toolbox (v2.0.0) (Wang et al., 2015) based on SPM12.
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing pipeline was GRETNA v2.0.0 (based on SPM12).

evidence_spans.text: Compared with healthy controls, children with ASD showed decreased effective connectivity among some large- scale brain networks. These brain networks included VN, DMN, cerebellum, SMN, and FPN.
evidence_spans.claim: Main finding: ASD children showed decreased (hypo) effective connectivity involving VN, DMN, cerebellum, SMN and FPN relative to TC.

assessments.support: IQ cutoff (WISC full scale IQ > 80) and medical/neurological exclusion criteria stated for the KKI/ABIDE II site.
Single site (KKI), age range 8-13, N by group before and after exclusion given, demographic Table 1 referenced.
GRETNA v2.0.0/SPM12 preprocessing steps (slice timing, realignment, normalization, smoothing) explicitly described.
ADOS scores used for correlation but the diagnostic instrument establishing case status is not explicitly restated in this report beyond citing the ABIDE II KKI dataset.

Groups age-matched and single-site (no cross-site confound), but sex/IQ matching and motion covariate handling in the spDCM/PEB model are not detailed beyond an exclusion threshold for 'excessive' motion that is not quantified.
Children with poor normalization/excessive head motion were excluded, but no explicit FD threshold value is reported.
Effective connectivity estimated with spectral DCM and second-level PEB, an established and described analysis pipeline.
PEB group-level inference and correlation analyses reported, but explicit multiple-comparison correction method for the connectivity/clinical correlations is not detailed in the sections read.

risk_of_bias.summary: Single-site (KKI/ABIDE II) group-difference study with well-described cohort and preprocessing, but motion threshold and multiple-comparison correction for behavioral correlations are not fully quantified.

charting.title: Attenuated effective connectivity of large-scale brain networks in children with autism spectrum disorders
charting.comorbidities_included_excluded: Excluded: definite neurological disease, severe chronic illness, severe visual impairment, alcohol/drug dependence; WISC-IV/V full-scale IQ > 80 required
charting.dataset_openly_available: No new dataset; data availability statement says contributions are in article/supplementary material, inquiries to corresponding authors (no participant list/code link found)
charting.specific_features: Spectral dynamic causal modelling (spDCM) effective connectivity among 24 AAL-template ROIs spanning 7 large-scale networks (VN, DMN, cerebellum, SMN, AN, SN, FPN)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: GRETNA v2.0.0 (SPM12) preprocessing; Group ICA of fMRI Toolbox (GIFT) for network identification; AAL atlas for ROI definition
charting.feature_change_direction: Decreased (attenuated) effective connectivity in ASD vs TC among VN, DMN, cerebellum, SMN and FPN; negative correlation between DMN(ANG_R)->SMN(PreCG_L) connectivity and ADOS stereotyped-behavior scores
charting.summary_key_findings: In 42 ASD and 127 TC children from the ABIDE II KKI site, SMN acted as a hub network in both groups; ASD children showed decreased effective connectivity among VN, DMN, cerebellum, SMN and FPN relative to TC, and DMN-to-SMN connectivity correlated negatively with ADOS stereotyped-behavior scores.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Attenuated effective connectivity among VN, DMN, cerebellum, SMN and FPN in ASD

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational); ABIDE II, KKI site only; n=42 ASD / 127 TC (ages 8-13), after excluding 14 ASD/28 TC.
narrative_row.methods: GRETNA v2.0.0 (SPM12) preprocessing; group ICA (GIFT) to identify 7 large-scale networks; 24 AAL-template ROIs; spectral DCM effective connectivity with PEB second-level group analysis.
narrative_row.outcomes: ASD children showed decreased effective connectivity among VN, DMN, cerebellum, SMN and FPN vs TC; DMN(ANG_R)-to-SMN(PreCG_L) connectivity negatively correlated with ADOS stereotyped-behavior scores.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Single site (KKI); no quantitative motion threshold reported; diagnostic-label source not restated in the analysed sections.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Demonstrates effective-connectivity (spDCM/PEB) analysis of the KKI subset of ABIDE II with AAL-based ROI definition.

kg_link.cohort_description: KKI site of ABIDE II; children aged 8-13 with WISC full-scale IQ>80, excluding neurological/chronic illness/substance dependence cases; 211 originally (56 ASD/155 TC), 14 ASD and 28 TC excluded for poor normalization, excessive motion or spDCM non-convergence, final n=42 ASD/127 TC.
kg_link.atlas: AAL (24 spherical ROIs across 7 large-scale networks)
kg_link.finding: ASD children showed decreased (attenuated) effective connectivity among VN, DMN, cerebellum, SMN and FPN relative to TC, with DMN(ANG_R)-to-SMN(PreCG_L) connectivity negatively correlated with ADOS stereotyped-behavior scores.
evidence_quotes: The subjects were 42 autistic children and 127 age-matched normal children from the ABIDE II dataset.
Compared with healthy controls, children with ASD showed decreased effective connectivity among some large- scale brain networks. These brain networks included VN, DMN, cerebellum, SMN, and FPN.
